title: Causal Ordering and Height-Balanced Invariants in a Compiler--Build System Communication Graph
topic: Communication Between the Compiler, the Build System, and Beyond
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: The communication between a compiler and its build system can be modeled as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of dependency nodes. This paper presents a C implementation that maintains a height-balanced search structure for node lookup and enforces strict key ordering during graph construction. We prove that insertion, deletion, and search operations run in $O(\log N)$ time, and that the topological sort algorithm preserves a causal ordering invariant. Static analysis of the source confirms that the graph data structure satisfies the required invariants and that the AST exhibits a balanced tree profile with a depth of $\log_2 N$. No runtime measurements were performed; all results are derived from formal proofs and static inspection. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261010_050648_communication_between_the_comp}
